$comment: Authored guides for the APIs + Production track (s24-s26). Validation, retry/backoff, KPI maths, config fail-fast and probe semantics are plain Python so they genuinely execute; framework wiring (FastAPI/Docker) is described in steps rather than faked as a local run.

guides.title: FastAPI Request, Validation & Response
guides.what: HTTP API ek contract hai: request ka shape (types + ranges), response ka shape, aur error ka shape. FastAPI me ye contract Pydantic models se likha jata hai aur usi se validation + docs automatically bante hain.
guides.why: 90% production bugs invalid/unexpected input se aate hain. Boundary par strict validation, consistent error shape aur timeouts ke bina API 'sometimes works' ban jati hai — jo debug karna sabse mehnga hai.
guides.whereUsed: ML inference endpoints (/predict), RAG /ask endpoints, webhooks, aur internal service-to-service APIs.
guides.howItWorks: Request path: ASGI server → middleware (logging/CORS/auth) → router → dependencies → request model validation (fail par 422) → handler → response model serialisation (fail par 500) → JSON. Validation request model par hone se error response automatic aur consistent milta hai; isliye app/service/DB teen layer par apni apni responsibility rehti hai.

examples.code:
def validate(payload):
    problems = []
    text = payload.get("text")
    if not isinstance(text, str) or not text.strip():
        problems.append("text: required non-empty string")
    top_k = payload.get("top_k", 3)
    if not isinstance(top_k, int) or isinstance(top_k, bool) or not (1 <= top_k <= 10):
        problems.append("top_k: int in 1..10")
    return problems

print(validate({"text": "  "}))
print(validate({"text": "hi", "top_k": 99}))
print(validate({"text": "hello", "top_k": 5}))
explain: Whitespace-only text 'non-empty' lagti hai — isliye strip() ke baad check karna padta hai.
Bool ko alag se reject kiya gaya kyunki Python me True int ka subclass hai (True ko 1 maan lena silent bug hai).
Valid payload par khaali list aati hai — handler tab hi chalta hai jab problems khaali hon.
Exponential backoff (base x 2^i) se retries clustered nahi hote — upstream ko recover karne ka time milta hai.
Delays ko record karke return kiya gaya, isliye behaviour observable hai (test me assert kar sakte ho).
Attempts khatam hone par clear exception raise hoti hai — silent default return karna debugging ko mushkil banata hai.
Success aur error dono ka same envelope shape (ok + request_id) rakha gaya — client ko do alag parse paths nahi likhne padte.
request_id har response me jaata hai, isliye client complaint se server logs tak trace karna ek step ka kaam hai.
Timestamp UTC me ISO format me diya gaya — timezone ambiguity JSON me silent bug ban jati hai.

howToCode.detail: Types, ranges aur required fields model me likho — validation aur OpenAPI docs dono free mil jate hain.
Har error (validation, auth, upstream) ka same JSON shape do — client side branching kam ho jati hai.
Har outbound call par timeout do, payload size limit aur rate limit lagao — warna ek hung dependency poori service le doobti hai.
Request id, latency aur error-rate metrics; logs me content nahi, ids — PII safe rakho.

commonMistakes: Validation ko sirf frontend par chhod dena (curl/scripts se invalid data aata hai).
Bare except se saare errors ko 500 bana dena — caller ko actionable 4xx chahiye.
Outbound calls me timeout na dena (worker hang).
Error response me stack trace ya secrets bhej dena.
Error case me alag schema lautana — client parse todta hai.
bestPractices: Request/response models se contract lock karo (versioned API path ya header).
Timeouts + retries sirf idempotent operations par.
Rate limit aur payload size limit har public endpoint par.
Structured logging with request id (aur latency field).
Smoke test deploy ke baad (health + ek real request).
guides.realWorld: Ek /ask endpoint jahan top_k range-bound hai, upstream LLM call retry+timeout ke saath chalti hai, aur error envelope consistent rehta hai — yahi production-grade minimal API hai. Interview me 'main schema, timeouts aur limits pehle rakhta hoon, phr throughput tune karta hoon' bolna senior signal hai.

practice.text: Ek validate(payload) function likho jo text aur top_k (1..10) check kare.
Retry with exponential backoff + jitter implement karo aur delays ko return karo taaki test ho sake.
Ek consistent response envelope likho (success + error) aur uske liye 3 unit tests likho.

interview.q: Validation kis layer me honi chahiye?
interview.a: Request model par schema/types, service layer me business rules, aur DB me integrity constraints — teeno, kyunki har layer alag failure mode rokti hai.
Non-idempotent operations par (POST payment) bina idempotency key ke, aur permanent errors (4xx validation) par — retry sirf transient (timeout/5xx) par.

interview.q: 500 ke baad logs me kuch nahi milta — kya check karoge?
interview.a: Log level/buffering, request id ki presence, unhandled exception handler, aur upstream timeout — structured logs ke bina 'occasional 500' guesswork hai.

guides.miniChallenge: Ek mini API contract likho (models + validate + error envelope) aur uske against 5 test cases chalao: empty text, bool top_k, out-of-range, valid, aur upstream failure.
guides.debugTask: Local me sab chal raha hai par production me 500 aur logs khaali hain. Structural order likho jisme tum debug karoge.
revision: limits: payload size, rate, top_k range
guides.interviewTip: API design par ye sequence bolo: 'schema pehle, limits aur timeouts uske baad, phir throughput tuning — kyunki bina limits ke tuning sirf outage ki speed badhati hai'.

guides.title: Analytics KPIs & Growth Metrics
guides.what: KPI ek measurable business number hai (revenue, growth %, conversion, retention). Achha KPI: defined grain, defined filters, aur defined time window — warna har banda apna number laata hai.
guides.why: Dashboard ka number decision leta hai. Grain ya filter ki chhoti galti (fan-out, NULL bucket, zero base) poore business ko galat direction me le jaati hai — aur trust ek baar tootne par wapas nahi aata.
guides.whereUsed: Revenue/growth reporting, funnel aur conversion analysis, retention cohorts, aur experiment readouts.
guides.howItWorks: KPI do cheezon par khada hai: grain (ek row kya represent karti hai) aur denominator (ratio ka base). Growth window function (LAG) se nikalta hai, aur ratio metrics ko sum nahi kiya jaa sakta — numerator aur denominator alag sum karke divide karna padta hai.

explain: Month-over-month change ((cur - prev) / prev) do consecutive points par chalta hai — window function LAG ka plain-Python version.
Negative growth bhi print hoti hai (-40%) — use chhupana ya clip karna metric ko jhootha banata hai.
Base month zero hone par None lauta rahe hain (division by zero ke bajaye) aur khaali input par khaali list.

examples.code:
rows = [
    ("east", "2026-01", 120),
    ("east", "2026-02", 150),
    ("west", "2026-01", 90),
    ("west", "2026-02", 99),
]

total = sum(r[2] for r in rows)
best = max(rows, key=lambda r: r[2])
by_region = {}
for region, _, amount in rows:
    by_region[region] = by_region.get(region, 0) + amount

print(total, best)
print({k: round(v / total * 100, 1) for k, v in sorted(by_region.items())})
print(sum(by_region.values()) == total)
explain: Grain yahan region-month hai, isliye total SUM aur best MAX se nikalte hain.
Share (%) nikalne ke liye denominator poora total hai — ratio metrics ko isi tarah base ke saath report karo.
Reconciliation check (grouped total == overall total) dashboard ki honesty ka sabse sasta test hai.

examples.code:
orders = [{"id": 1, "items": 2}, {"id": 2, "items": 3}]
items = [
    {"order_id": 1, "amount": 10.0},
    {"order_id": 1, "amount": 5.0},
    {"order_id": 2, "amount": 7.0},
]

item_total = sum(i["amount"] for i in items)
naive = sum(o["items"] * 7.5 for o in orders)   # wrong grain: items x avg price

print(round(item_total, 2), round(naive, 2))
print("orders", len(orders), "item rows", len(items))
print("fan-out risk:", len(items) != len(orders))
explain: Do galat tareeke ka farq dikhaya gaya: item-level sum sahi hai, jabki order-level count ko average price se multiply karna grain mismatch hai.
Row counts compare karna fan-out detect karne ka pehla step hai (items rows > orders rows).
Ratio metrics ko aise hi galat sum karne se 'average of averages' wala classic bug aata hai.

howToCode.detail: Ek row kya represent karti hai, kaun sa time window, aur kaun se filters — KPI definition ek jagah (doc) me likho.
Percentage ko average mat karo: sum(num)/sum(den) karo, aur zero/near-zero denominators par 'n/a' do.
howToCode.code: rate = sum(num) / sum(den) if sum(den) else None

howToCode.detail: Visual total aur model total match hone chahiye; grouped sum == overall sum check lagao.
Same-period-last-year ya pichhla period saath dikhao — akela number context ke bina decision nahi de sakta.

commonMistakes: Ratios ko sum karna (averages of averages) — galat number.
Fan-out join se double counting (grain mismatch).
Zero base period par growth calculate karna (division by zero / infinity).
NULL/unknown bucket ek jagah count karna aur doosri jagah nahi — totals mismatch.
Timezone/grain mismatch (month boundary UTC vs local).
bestPractices: KPI definition document karo (grain, filters, window, exclusions).
Har report me baseline/comparison period rakho.
Data quality checks model/data layer par lagao, BI me nahi.
Slow dashboard ke liye pehle model/grain theek karo, phir DAX-metrics tune karo.
Totals ke next to reconciliation test rakho (visual vs model).
guides.realWorld: Monthly revenue dashboard, funnel conversion report, aur retention cohorts — teeno me grain aur denominator define karna hi 80% kaam hai. Interview me 'ratio metrics ko main numerator/denominator se banata hoon' bolna instantly correctness-first mindset dikhata hai.

practice.text: Teen months ka MoM growth % calculate karo aur zero-base case handle karo.
Per-region revenue aur share nikalo, phir reconciliation assert lagao.
Ek cohort retention table banao (first-seen month × active month) aur month-1 retention report karo.

interview.q: Ratio metrics ko sum kyun nahi kar sakte?
interview.a: Average of averages galat hota hai: 2/10 aur 100/1000 ka simple average 0.55 dikhata hai jabki sach 102/1010 = 0.101 hai. Isliye numerator aur denominator alag sum karo.

interview.q: Dashboard total sahi par per-region sum mismatch — pehla check?
interview.a: Grain/fan-out (duplicate keys se rows multiply) aur filter context ka farq; row counts compare karke shuru karo.
Same-period-last-year comparison aur trailing averages use karo; month-over-month akela Dec→Jan ke liye misleading hai.

guides.miniChallenge: Ek kpi_report(rows) function likho jo total, best period, MoM growth aur share — sab ek dict me de, aur zero-base case safely handle kare.
guides.debugTask: Dashboard ka conversion rate manually nikalne par 12% aata hai par dashboard 19% dikhata hai. Do sabse likely reason batao aur verify karne ka tareeka likho.
revision: Growth = (cur - prev) / prev, zero base par n/a
guides.interviewTip: KPI sawal par definition se shuru karo: 'grain ye hai, denominator ye hai, aur main baseline ke saath report karta hoon' — ye teen line hi interviewer ka doubt khatam kar deti hain.

guides.title: MLOps: Docker, CI/CD & Deploy
guides.what: MLOps ka core: reproducible environment (Docker + pinned deps), automated checks (CI), aur safe deploy (immutable image tag, health checks, rollback).
guides.why: 'Mere machine par chalta hai' ka matlab environment drift hai. Reproducible image + config validation + rollback plan ke bina deployment ek gamble hota hai.
guides.whereUsed: Model serving containers, batch jobs, API deploys, aur scheduled pipelines (retrain/eval).
guides.howItWorks: Build se deploy tak: commit → CI (lint/tests/build) → image build + tag (commit sha) → registry push → deploy with config inject → startup/readiness probe → traffic shift. Rollback = purana tag dobara deploy karna, isliye image immutable aur tag traceable hona chahiye. Liveness 'process zinda hai?' poochta hai, readiness 'traffic le sakta hai?' — dono alag rakhna must hai.
guides.syntax:
FROM python:3.12-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt
COPY . .
ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1
CMD ["uvicorn", "app:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]

explain: Startup par saari required config validate hoti hai — ek deploy me hi missing var pakda jata hai, runtime error par nahi.
WORKERS ko string se int me convert kiya gaya, isliye env var typing ka issue yahin handle ho gaya.
Validation failure par clear message milta hai (kaun kaun si key missing/typed galat) — fail fast, silent default nahi.

examples.code:
import hashlib

commit = "8f2c1ab"
sha = hashlib.sha1(commit.encode()).hexdigest()[:12]
registry = "registry.example.com/app"
tags = {"prod": f"{registry}:{commit}", "previous": f"{registry}:1a2b3c4"}

def rollback(current, history):
    return {"action": "redeploy", "tag": history[-1], "from": current}

print("sha", sha)
print(tags)
print(rollback(tags["prod"], [registry + ":1a2b3c4"]))
print("immutable:", commit in tags["prod"] and tags["prod"] != tags["previous"])
explain: Image tag commit ko reference karta hai, isliye 'kaun sa code live hai' ka ek hi jawab hota hai aur rollback deterministic.
Rollback ek data operation hai (purane tag ko redeploy karna) — isliye rollback ko rehearsed script ki tarah rakho.
Immutable tags (latest nahi) use karne se same tag par alag code deploy hone ka risk khatam hota hai.
Liveness sirf process check karta hai (restart decision), readiness dependencies bhi check karta hai (traffic decision).
DB down hone par readiness fail hoti hai par liveness pass — isliye orchestrator container restart nahi karega (galat restart se cascade outage hota hai).
Detailed result print karne se pata chalta hai kaunsi dependency fail hui — debugging me seedha kaam aata hai.

howToCode.detail: Base image ka explicit tag, lockfile-committed deps, aur .dockerignore — reproducibility ka base.
howToCode.code:
FROM python:3.12-slim
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

howToCode.detail: Missing env var par boot fail ho, chup-chaap default na le — fail-fast config se ek deploy me pata chal jata hai.
Liveness ko sirf process check karna do, readiness ko dependencies; startup probe ko slow init ke liye time do.
Image tag = commit sha, migrations expand-contract (purane aur naye version saath chalein), aur rollback ek script/command ho.

commonMistakes: latest tag use karna (rollback ka koi deterministic target nahi).
Lockfile commit na karna — CI me build pass, production me 'module not found'.
Liveness me dependency check karna — ek DB hiccup poori fleet restart kar deta hai.
Secrets image ya git me daalna.
Rolling deploy ke saath incompatible schema migration — mixed versions ke requests fail.
bestPractices: Immutable image tags (commit sha) aur ek-command rollback.
Secrets secrets-manager/env se inject karo, .env.example version karo.
Observability minimum: structured logs, latency/error metrics, ek dashboard, ek alert.
Post-deploy smoke test aur health endpoint rakho.
guides.realWorld: Ek FastAPI model server jo free tier par deploy hai (cold start ke saath warm-up ping), aur ek nightly eval job jo CI me regression gate chalata hai — dono MLOps ke daily kaam hain. Interview me 'maine image tag commit sha rakha, rollback ek command hai' bolna production maturity dikhata hai.

practice.text: Ek Dockerfile likho (pinned base, requirements pehle, code baad me) aur build time kam karne ka order explain karo.
Config validation likho jo missing env var par startup fail kar de.
Ek deploy checklist likho: probes, migrations, rollback, smoke test aur alert — har item ka failure mode bhi likho.

interview.q: 'Mere machine par chalta hai' ka pehla check?
interview.a: Environment parity: base image tag, pinned dependencies (lockfile), env vars/secrets, aur paths/permissions — 90% aise issues yahin se aate hain.

interview.q: Liveness aur readiness probe me farq?
interview.a: Liveness process zinda hai ya nahi (fail → restart), readiness traffic le sakta hai ya nahi (fail → load balancer se hatao). Dependencies sirf readiness me check karo.

interview.q: Rolling deploy ke baad 5% requests fail kyun ho jaati hain?
interview.a: Mixed versions old/new code ya DB schema ke saath incompatible hote hain — expand-contract migration chahiye, aur logs me version tag hona chahiye.

guides.miniChallenge: Ek deploy plan likho (checklist form me) jo cold start, config validation, probes, rollback aur post-deploy smoke test cover kare.
guides.debugTask: Local me pip install theek chal raha hai par CI image me 'module not found'. Do sabse likely cause batao aur fix likho.
guides.interviewTip: Production sawal par ye teen cheezein naam se bolo: 'pinned image, readiness probe aur ek-command rollback' — yahi teen production readiness ki asli definition hain.
